ai.description: This small frog reaches 22–26 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark interorbital bar and granular skin. It features a pale, cream-colored belly and lacks webbing on the fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Honnametti Bush Frog is best distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow-orange coloration on its hidden groin and inner thigh areas, which contrasts sharply with its body.
ai.habitat: The Honnametti Bush Frog inhabits the mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found between 1,200 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Honnametti bush frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in dense foliage during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes honnametti* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Honnametti Bush Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests in the Biligiriranga Hills.
ai.callDescription: The Honnametti Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from the canopy of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats.
